html:
The Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions is an interfaith meeting held every three years in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, since 2003. It was the idea of President Nursultan Nazarbayev.

It brings together leaders of Islam, Christianity, Judaism, Buddhism, Hinduism, Shinto, Taoism and other faiths, along with politicians and heads of international bodies, to talk about peace and tolerance. Pope Francis attended in 2022. Since 2006 it has met in the Palace of Peace and Reconciliation, the glass pyramid built for it.

Kazakhstan, home to many peoples, mostly Muslim with a large Orthodox Christian minority, uses the congress to present itself as a bridge between East and West and a model of religious peace. Critics point out that the same state keeps tight control over religious groups at home. It echoes an old custom of steppe rulers, such as the Mongol khans who hosted debates between faiths, as William of Rubruck saw at Karakorum.
sum: The Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions is an interfaith meeting held every three years in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, since 2003. It was the idea of President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
